triage.name: Vaginal Bleeding
triage.reason: Common symptom presentation with broad differential (pregnancy, fibroids, malignancy, anovulatory bleeding) that requires structured history, exam and testing.

review_issues: presentation: older format without SNOMED terms
exam: older format without SNOMED terms

demographics: Affects women across the lifespan; premenopausal women most often present with heavy, prolonged or intermenstrual bleeding, while postmenopausal women present with any bleeding after menopause
More common in the perimenopausal years as cycles become anovulatory
Obesity, nulliparity and chronic anovulation are associated with endometrial pathology

risk_factors.text: Polycystic ovary syndrome or chronic anovulation
Use of hormonal contraception or hormone therapy

comorbidities: Von Willebrand disease or other bleeding disorder

chief_complaints.text: My periods have gotten much heavier

hpi.onset: Variable; may be gradual over several cycles or sudden, depending on the cause
hpi.duration: From a single episode to months of abnormal bleeding
hpi.progression: Often persistent or recurrent; may worsen over time with structural causes such as fibroids or polyps, or fluctuate with hormonal causes
hpi.location: Vaginal bleeding; pelvic cramping or pressure may accompany it
hpi.radiation: Pelvic pain may radiate to the lower back or thighs
hpi.quality: Bleeding may be light spotting, heavy flow with clots, or continuous
hpi.severity: Ranges from spotting to heavy bleeding causing anemia, dizziness or fatigue
hpi.timing: May occur between periods, after intercourse, or after menopause; heavy periods may last longer than 7 days

associated_symptoms.text: Feeling of pelvic pressure or fullness
Hot flashes or night sweats if perimenopausal

pertinent_negatives: Bleeding from other sites such as gums or easy bruising
Recent dilation and curettage or uterine procedure

atypical.how_it_differs: Bleeding before puberty is abnormal and may indicate precocious puberty, foreign body, trauma or infection; the child may not describe bleeding and it is noticed on underwear or toilet paper.
Postmenopausal bleeding is often painless and may be minimal; malignancy must be excluded even with a single episode.

Bleeding in pregnancy may signal miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy, placenta previa or abruption; it requires urgent evaluation and the presentation may include abdominal pain, passage of tissue or hemodynamic instability.
Chronic anovulation and excess estrogen increase risk of endometrial hyperplasia and cancer; bleeding may be chronic and heavy without cyclical pattern.

general.moderate: Mildly pale, fatigued but not distressed
general.severe: Pale, tachycardic, lightheaded on standing, visibly fatigued
general.critical: Ill-appearing, pale and diaphoretic, lethargic or confused, may be hypotensive

findings.maneuver: Inspect the conjunctivae and oral mucosa
findings.finding: Conjunctival or mucosal pallor suggesting anemia from blood loss

findings.maneuver: Palpate the radial pulse or auscultate the heart rate
Measure blood pressure and pulse supine and after standing
findings.finding: Orthostatic drop in blood pressure or rise in pulse, indicating significant volume loss

findings.maneuver: Palpate all four quadrants of the abdomen
findings.finding: Suprapubic or diffuse lower abdominal tenderness

findings.maneuver: Palpate the lower abdomen and suprapubic region
findings.finding: Palpable suprapubic mass, suggesting an enlarged uterus or pelvic mass

findings.maneuver: Perform a speculum examination and inspect the vaginal vault and cervix
findings.finding: Blood in the vaginal vault or visible bleeding from the cervical os

findings.maneuver: Inspect the cervix with a speculum
findings.finding: Visible cervical lesion, polyp, erosion or friable mass

findings.maneuver: Perform a bimanual examination to assess uterine size, shape and mobility
findings.finding: Enlarged, irregular or boggy uterus suggesting fibroids or other uterine pathology

findings.maneuver: Move the cervix gently during bimanual examination
Move the cervix gently during bimanual examination
Perform a digital rectal examination when gastrointestinal bleeding is a consideration
findings.finding: No gross blood on the examining glove, normal rectal tone

findings.maneuver: Inspect the skin for petechiae, ecchymoses or other bleeding signs

labs.caveat: Must be checked in any woman of reproductive age before imaging or procedures; a positive result redirects the workup toward pregnancy-related causes such as ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage, placenta previa or abruption.
Anemia reflects the severity and chronicity of blood loss; a normal hemoglobin does not exclude significant acute bleeding early on.
Thrombocytopenia suggests a bleeding disorder or systemic illness rather than a purely structural cause.
Low MCV suggests iron deficiency from chronic blood loss.
Low ferritin confirms iron deficiency from chronic blood loss; ferritin is an acute phase reactant and may be falsely normal in inflammation.
Both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism can cause abnormal uterine bleeding.
Prolonged in coagulopathy, liver disease or with warfarin use.
Prolonged in von Willebrand disease, factor deficiencies or heparin use.
Low in disseminated intravascular coagulation or severe hemorrhage.
Elevated from prerenal azotemia due to volume loss.
Rises with hypovolemia from heavy bleeding.
Blood in the urine may reflect contamination from vaginal bleeding or a separate urinary source.

findings.finding: Sinus tachycardia from anemia, hypovolemia or pain
Diffuse ST depression or T-wave flattening from severe anemia and demand ischemia

imaging.preferred_when: First-line for most premenopausal and postmenopausal women with abnormal uterine bleeding

findings.text: Endometrial thickness measured; thin and uniform in normal postmenopausal women
Thickened or irregular endometrium suggesting hyperplasia or malignancy
Normal study with no structural cause identified

imaging.preferred_when: When transvaginal ultrasound is nondiagnostic and focal intrauterine lesions are suspected

findings.text: Focal intracavitary filling defect consistent with endometrial polyp
Submucosal fibroid distorting the endometrial cavity
Smooth endometrial lining without focal lesion

imaging.preferred_when: Postmenopausal bleeding, or premenopausal bleeding with risk factors for endometrial cancer

findings.text: Proliferative or secretory endometrium consistent with benign hormonal bleeding
Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia or endometrial carcinoma

imaging.preferred_when: Direct visualization and biopsy of focal intrauterine lesions

imaging.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.preferred_when: Not first-line for vaginal bleeding; used when a pelvic mass, malignancy or extrauterine source is suspected

findings.text: Pelvic mass or lymphadenopathy suggesting malignancy

imaging.study: Pelvic MRI without and with contrast
imaging.preferred_when: Problem solving for fibroid mapping, adenomyosis or suspected malignancy

findings.text: Leiomyomas characterized by location and size

initial.why: Rules out pregnancy and pregnancy-related bleeding before any imaging or procedure
Assesses severity of blood loss and anemia
Evaluates volume status and renal function
Thyroid dysfunction is a reversible cause of abnormal uterine bleeding
Screens for coagulopathy, especially with heavy bleeding since menarche
Screens for coagulopathy, especially with heavy bleeding since menarche
Confirms iron deficiency from chronic blood loss
initial.only_if: anemia or chronic heavy bleeding is present

initial.why: First-line imaging to identify fibroids, polyps, endometrial thickening or adnexal masses

confirmatory.why: Confirms or excludes endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma
confirmatory.only_if: postmenopausal bleeding, or premenopausal bleeding with risk factors for endometrial cancer

confirmatory.why: Directly visualizes and biopsies focal intrauterine lesions
confirmatory.only_if: focal lesion is seen on ultrasound or biopsy is nondiagnostic
transvaginal ultrasound is nondiagnostic and a polyp or submucosal fibroid is suspected

supporting.why: Supports an inflammatory or infectious process when pelvic infection is considered
Nonspecific marker of inflammation or malignancy

supporting.test: Pelvic MRI without and with contrast
supporting.why: Problem solving for fibroid mapping, adenomyosis or suspected malignancy
supporting.only_if: ultrasound is inconclusive or malignancy is suspected

not_indicated.test: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
not_indicated.why: Not first-line for vaginal bleeding; exposes the patient to radiation and is less sensitive for intrauterine pathology
No role in the evaluation of vaginal bleeding
Not needed unless abdominal pain suggests pancreatitis
Not routinely needed; may be contaminated by vaginal blood

decision_points: Pregnancy test before any imaging or procedure in a woman of reproductive age
Postmenopausal bleeding requires endometrial sampling to exclude cancer even if ultrasound is normal
Hemodynamically unstable patients need resuscitation and urgent gynecology involvement before imaging
Transvaginal ultrasound is first-line; reserve CT for suspected extrauterine or malignant disease

differential.name: Ectopic pregnancy
differential.why_considered: Vaginal bleeding in a woman of reproductive age, especially with pelvic pain or a missed period
differential.trigger: Any woman of reproductive age with vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain, or a positive pregnancy test

history: History of pelvic inflammatory disease, prior ectopic or tubal surgery
imaging: No intrauterine pregnancy on transvaginal ultrasound
Adnexal mass or free fluid in the pelvis

differential.name: Endometrial cancer
differential.why_considered: Postmenopausal bleeding or persistent intermenstrual bleeding, especially with obesity or chronic anovulation
differential.trigger: Any bleeding after menopause, or persistent abnormal bleeding in a woman with risk factors

history: Chronic anovulation or polycystic ovary syndrome
Family history of endometrial or colon cancer
exam: Possible enlarged uterus or visible cervical lesion
imaging: Thickened or irregular endometrium on transvaginal ultrasound
Endometrial biopsy showing hyperplasia with atypia or carcinoma

differential.name: Cervical cancer
differential.why_considered: Postcoital bleeding, intermenstrual bleeding or a friable cervical lesion
differential.trigger: Bleeding after intercourse or a visible cervical lesion on speculum exam

history: History of abnormal cervical screening or no recent screening
exam: Visible cervical lesion, erosion or friable mass
imaging: Hydronephrosis or pelvic lymphadenopathy if advanced

differential.name: Uterine fibroids
differential.why_considered: Heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding with pelvic pressure or an enlarged uterus

labs: Anemia or low ferritin from chronic blood loss
imaging: Well-defined hypoechoic myometrial masses on transvaginal ultrasound

differential.name: Endometrial polyps
differential.why_considered: Intermenstrual bleeding or postmenopausal spotting with a focal intracavitary lesion

exam: Possible cervical polyp visible at the os
imaging: Focal echogenic endometrial lesion on transvaginal ultrasound
Intracavitary filling defect on saline infusion sonohysterography

differential.name: Anovulatory uterine bleeding
differential.why_considered: Irregular, unpredictable bleeding in perimenopause or with polycystic ovary syndrome

exam: Signs of hyperandrogenism if polycystic ovary syndrome
labs: Endometrial biopsy shows benign proliferative endometrium
imaging: Normal transvaginal ultrasound without structural lesion

differential.name: Coagulopathy or bleeding disorder
differential.why_considered: Heavy bleeding since menarche, bleeding from other sites or a family history of bleeding disorders

differential.name: Thyroid dysfunction
differential.why_considered: Abnormal uterine bleeding with systemic symptoms of thyroid disease

differential.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
differential.why_considered: Bleeding from the lower gastrointestinal tract may be mistaken for vaginal bleeding

exam: No blood in the vaginal vault on speculum exam
imaging: Colonoscopy or upper endoscopy identifies the source

severity.mild: Light spotting or slightly heavy periods without anemia or hemodynamic compromise; patient is comfortable and well-appearing
severity.moderate: Heavy or prolonged bleeding with mild anemia, fatigue and tachycardia but stable blood pressure
severity.severe: Heavy bleeding with significant anemia, orthostatic hypotension, dizziness and resting tachycardia
severity.critical: Exsanguinating hemorrhage with hemodynamic instability, altered mental status or shock requiring immediate resuscitation and transfusion

red_flags.meaning: Ectopic pregnancy or pregnancy-related bleeding until proven otherwise; requires urgent evaluation

red_flags.finding: Hemodynamic instability, syncope or heart rate over 120
red_flags.meaning: Significant blood loss or ruptured ectopic pregnancy; needs immediate resuscitation and gynecology involvement
Endometrial cancer must be excluded even with a single episode

red_flags.finding: Visible friable cervical lesion or postcoital bleeding
red_flags.meaning: Cervical cancer or other cervical pathology; requires biopsy

red_flags.finding: Severe one-sided pelvic pain with bleeding
red_flags.meaning: Ectopic pregnancy or ovarian torsion; surgical emergency

red_flags.finding: Bleeding with fever and purulent discharge
red_flags.meaning: Pelvic inflammatory disease or endometritis; requires antibiotics

complications.name: Infertility or recurrent pregnancy loss
clues: Untreated fibroids or polyps distorting the cavity

special_populations.differences: Bleeding before puberty is abnormal and may indicate precocious puberty, foreign body, trauma or infection; the child may not describe bleeding and it is noticed on underwear or toilet paper.
Postmenopausal bleeding is often painless and may be minimal; malignancy must be excluded even with a single episode.

Bleeding in pregnancy may signal miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy, placenta previa or abruption; it requires urgent evaluation and the presentation may include abdominal pain, passage of tissue or hemodynamic instability.
Chronic anovulation and excess estrogen increase risk of endometrial hyperplasia and cancer; bleeding may be chronic and heavy without cyclical pattern.

key_questions.question: Could you be pregnant? When was your last menstrual period?
key_questions.looking_for: Any possibility of pregnancy; a positive or uncertain pregnancy status redirects the workup toward ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage, placenta previa or abruption

key_questions.question: When did the bleeding start, and how has it changed since then?
key_questions.looking_for: Sudden onset suggests acute bleeding from a structural or pregnancy-related cause; gradual onset over cycles suggests hormonal or structural causes

key_questions.question: How heavy is the bleeding — how many pads or tampons per day, and are you passing clots?
key_questions.looking_for: Soaking a pad or tampon every hour, large clots or bleeding lasting more than 7 days indicates heavy menstrual bleeding and risk of anemia

key_questions.question: Is the bleeding between periods, after intercourse, or after menopause?
key_questions.looking_for: Postmenopausal bleeding requires exclusion of endometrial cancer; postcoital bleeding suggests cervical pathology

key_questions.question: Have you had any dizziness, lightheadedness, palpitations or fainting?
key_questions.looking_for: Symptoms of significant blood loss or anemia requiring urgent resuscitation

key_questions.question: Do you have pelvic pain or cramping, and if so, is it one-sided or diffuse?
key_questions.looking_for: Severe one-sided pain suggests ectopic pregnancy or ovarian torsion; cramping suggests fibroids or passage of tissue

key_questions.question: Have you ever been told you have fibroids, polyps, endometriosis or a bleeding disorder?
key_questions.looking_for: Known structural uterine pathology or coagulopathy explaining recurrent bleeding

key_questions.question: Are you using any hormonal contraception, hormone therapy or tamoxifen?
key_questions.looking_for: Hormonal pills, depot medroxyprogesterone, hormone therapy and tamoxifen are common causes of abnormal bleeding

key_questions.question: Are you taking any blood thinners such as warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban or aspirin?
key_questions.looking_for: Anticoagulation or antiplatelet therapy increases bleeding severity and may be the primary cause

key_questions.question: Have you had heavy periods since you first started menstruating, or easy bruising and bleeding gums?
key_questions.looking_for: Bleeding since menarche with other bleeding sites suggests von Willebrand disease or another coagulopathy

key_questions.question: Is there any chance you have been exposed to a sexually transmitted infection, or have you had abnormal vaginal discharge?
key_questions.looking_for: Purulent discharge or a new partner suggests pelvic inflammatory disease or cervicitis, which can cause bleeding

key_questions.question: Has anyone in your family had uterine fibroids, endometrial or ovarian cancer, or a bleeding disorder?
key_questions.looking_for: Family history of fibroids, gynecologic cancer or bleeding disorders raises suspicion for those causes

key_questions.question: Have you had any unintentional weight loss, night sweats or fevers?
key_questions.looking_for: Constitutional symptoms raise concern for malignancy or systemic infection

key_questions.question: Have you had any blood in your stool, black stools or rectal bleeding separate from your periods?
key_questions.looking_for: Gastrointestinal bleeding can be mistaken for vaginal bleeding and requires a separate workup

key_questions.question: Have you ever had a dilation and curettage, uterine procedure or pelvic radiation?
key_questions.looking_for: Recent uterine instrumentation or prior pelvic radiation can cause bleeding and alter the differential

reasoning_points: Pregnancy status is established first in any woman of reproductive age before imaging or procedures
The bleeding pattern is characterized by timing (intermenstrual, postcoital, postmenopausal), heaviness and duration
Hemodynamic stability and severity of blood loss are assessed with vital signs, orthostatics and hemoglobin
A pelvic examination with speculum inspection localizes the source and identifies cervical or vaginal lesions
Transvaginal ultrasound is first-line imaging to identify fibroids, polyps, endometrial thickening or adnexal masses
Postmenopausal bleeding requires endometrial sampling to exclude endometrial cancer even if ultrasound is normal
Reversible causes such as thyroid dysfunction, coagulopathy and hormonal medication are considered and tested for
Life-threatening causes such as ectopic pregnancy and exsanguinating hemorrhage are excluded early

easy: Reproductive-age woman with a positive pregnancy test and pelvic pain
Postmenopausal woman with a single episode of painless bleeding
Classic heavy periods with an enlarged, irregular uterus suggesting fibroids
Bleeding with clear hormonal trigger such as starting or missing birth control pills
medium: Perimenopausal woman with irregular, unpredictable bleeding and no structural lesion on ultrasound
Woman with postcoital spotting and a friable cervical lesion
Young woman with heavy bleeding since menarche and a family history of bleeding
Bleeding with mild anemia and fatigue but stable vital signs
hard: Hemodynamically unstable patient with heavy bleeding requiring resuscitation before imaging
Older adult with minimal postmenopausal spotting and a normal-appearing ultrasound
Bleeding attributed to hemorrhoids that is actually from a gynecologic or gastrointestinal source
Pregnant patient with painless bleeding and a low-lying placenta on ultrasound
Patient on anticoagulation with bleeding from multiple sites
